readOnly.title: You can see this connection, not change it
readOnly.description: Changing a connection needs the connection.write permission.

list.title: SSO
list.description: The SAML connections people sign in through, and the SAML apps Qeet ID signs them in to.

empty.title: No SAML connections or apps yet
empty.description: Add one below: people then sign in through your identity provider, or Qeet ID signs them in to an app.

emptyFiltered.title: No connections match
emptyFiltered.description: Nothing here matches the search or the view.

list.elsewhere: LDAP and SCIM connections are in

offers.label: Not set up yet
offers.saml: People sign in through Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace or another identity provider.
offers.app: Qeet ID signs your people in to another app, such as Slack or AWS.

links.title: Setup links
links.note: Let the IT admin who runs your identity provider set up SAML sign-in or SCIM provisioning, without a Qeet ID account.
links.samlNote: Add, change, test and delete SAML connections
links.scimNote: Make, replace and revoke the SCIM token
links.emptyDescription: A link works until it ends or you revoke it, and every change made with it is in the audit log.

create.title: Create a setup link
create.note: Whoever has the link can make these changes until it ends or you revoke it.
create.expiresNote: 24 hours at most: Qeet ID ends every link within a day.

made.title: Copy the setup link now
made.description: You won't see it again. Send it to your IT admin; it works until {{when}}.

revoke.title: Revoke this setup link?
revoke.description: Whoever has it can't make another change, from their next one. What they've already changed stays.

scim.title: SCIM provisioning
scim.description: Your identity provider adds, updates and removes people in {{org}}.

gate.title: SCIM provisioning isn't in your plan
gate.description: Upgrade to let your identity provider add and remove people here.

steps.label: Setting up SCIM
steps.details: Give your identity provider the details

how.title: How provisioning works
how.note: Your identity provider sends each change to Qeet ID's SCIM address, with the token. Nothing is read from it: it sends, Qeet ID applies.
how.idpNote: Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace or OneLogin, holding the token.
how.endpointNote: People and groups, as they change.
how.hereNote: New people only with an address on a domain {{org}} has verified.

details.title: Give your identity provider these details
details.note: Paste them into its SCIM app, then start provisioning there.
details.baseUrlHint: In Okta: SCIM connector base URL. In Entra ID: Tenant URL.
details.userNameHint: Each person's email address, sent as userName (or their primary email).

token.title: Token
token.note: Your identity provider presents it with every request. Qeet ID keeps only a hash of it and its first characters, so it's shown once, when it's made.
token.notSetHint: Make one, then paste it into your identity provider.
token.setHint: Making a new one stops this one at once.
token.usedHint: When your identity provider last sent a change with it.
token.linksHint: An open setup link with SCIM lets your IT admin replace or revoke this token.

fresh.title: Copy the token now
fresh.description: You won't see it again. Paste it into your identity provider; if it's lost, make a new one.

replace.title: Make a new SCIM token?
replace.description: The token your identity provider holds stops working at once. Changes stop arriving until you paste the new one into it.

revoke.zoneNote: Your identity provider can no longer send changes. The people it created stay as they are.
revoke.title: Revoke the SCIM token?
revoke.description_one: Your identity provider can no longer send changes here: new people, updates and suspensions stop until you give it a new token. The {{n}} person it created stays as they are.
revoke.description_other: Your identity provider can no longer send changes here: new people, updates and suspensions stop until you give it a new token. The {{n}} people it created stay as they are.

changes.title: When people change in your identity provider
changes.note: What each change it sends does here.
changes.addedText: They get an account in {{org}}, or the account already here with that email is linked. Only on a domain {{org}} has verified.
changes.deactivatedText: Suspended here, and every session and sign-in ends at once.
changes.deactivatedHint: Turning them back on there lifts only a suspension the identity provider set.
changes.removedText: Their account is deleted, and every session and sign-in ends.
changes.groupsText: Groups it sends are made here, and their members kept as it says.
changes.ownersText: It can't change, suspend or remove an owner of {{org}}.

people.title: People it provisioned
people.note: Made or linked by your identity provider, newest first.
people.emptyDescription: People appear here once your identity provider sends them.

gate.title: Directory sign-in isn't in your plan
gate.description: Upgrade to let people sign in with their LDAP or Active Directory password.

index.title: LDAP or Active Directory
index.description: People sign in with their directory name and password, and are added here the first time they do.
index.whatTitle: How sign-in through a directory works
index.whatNote: Nothing is copied from the directory: Qeet ID asks it each time someone signs in.

steps.bind: Qeet ID connects to your directory server with a read-only service account.
steps.find: It looks the person up under a base DN with a filter, by the name they typed.
steps.check: It checks their password by signing in to the directory as them.
steps.signIn: Their email and name come from directory attributes; the first time, they get an account here.

index.emptyDescription: Connect one: it starts as a draft, so nobody signs in with it until you've tested it and turned it on.

notFound.title: Connection not found
notFound.description: It may have been deleted. Directories › Connections lists every connection.

failing.title: Qeet ID can't sign in to {{host}}
failing.description: The latest test failed {{when}}: {{reason}}. Check the server address and the service account, then test again.

how.title: How a sign-in goes through it
how.note: Each time someone signs in, in this order, with this connection's settings.
how.label: A sign-in through this connection, step by step
how.bind: Sign in as the service account
how.bindNote: At {{host}} ({{how}}). Its password is kept encrypted and never shown again.
how.findNote: Under this base DN, with what they typed in place of %s. Exactly one entry must match, or the sign-in fails.
how.checkNote: Qeet ID signs in to the directory as the entry it found, with the password they typed. The password isn't kept.
how.signInNote: The first time, an account is made in {{org}}, only for an address on a domain {{org}} has verified.

server.title: Server
server.note: Where Qeet ID connects, and how.

encryptionHint.ldaps: The connection is encrypted before anything is sent.
encryptionHint.starttls: Qeet ID upgrades the connection to TLS before it signs in.
encryptionHint.none: Passwords cross the network unencrypted. Use ldaps://, or turn on StartTLS.

server.verifyHint: Qeet ID checks the server's certificate against its name.
server.skipHint: Only a developer workstation may skip the check; elsewhere Qeet ID refuses to connect.

attributes.title: Attributes
attributes.note: Which directory attributes become each person's email and name.
attributes.emailHint: Required: it matches people to their account here. An entry without it can't sign in.
attributes.name: Display name
attributes.nameHint: Their display name when their account is made here.
attributes.newPeopleText: Added to {{org}} the first time they sign in. An account already here is linked only if its address is verified and it doesn't administer {{org}}.

status.title: Status
status.note: Only a connection that's on signs anyone in.

means.draft: Being set up: it signs nobody in. Test it, then turn it on.
means.active: People sign in with their directory name and password.
means.disabled: Sign-ins are refused. People who signed in with it keep their accounts.

test.title: Test
test.note: The test connects to the server and signs in as the service account. It doesn't look anyone up.
test.check: Reach the server and sign in as the service account

failed.unreachable: Qeet ID couldn't reach the server. Check its address and that it accepts connections from Qeet ID.
failed.serviceAccount: The server refused the service account. Check its bind DN and password.
failed.certificate: The server's certificate must be checked. Give it one that can be, and don't skip the check.
failed.other: The test didn't pass. Try again, or check the connection's settings.

signIns.title: Sign-ins
signIns.none: No one has signed in with it yet.
signIns.counts: {{ok}} signed in, {{failed}} failed, in the last 30 days.
signIns.label: Sign-ins a day for 30 days: {{ok}} signed in, {{failed}} failed
signIns.empty: No sign-in attempts in the last 30 days.

drawer.title: Connect a directory
drawer.description: An LDAP or Active Directory server people sign in with. It starts as a draft unless you turn it on.
drawer.editDescription: Changes apply to the next sign-in.
drawer.name: Name
drawer.serverUrlHint: ldaps:// for TLS from the start, or ldap://. The port goes after the host.
drawer.startTlsHint: Upgrade an ldap:// connection to TLS before signing in.
drawer.startTlsLdaps: ldaps:// is already TLS from the start.
drawer.skipVerifyHint: Only on a developer workstation: elsewhere Qeet ID refuses to save or use it.
drawer.bindDnHint: A read-only account Qeet ID signs in as to look people up.
drawer.bindPasswordHint: Kept encrypted, and never shown again.
drawer.bindPasswordKeep: Leave it empty to keep the one saved.
drawer.baseDnHint: Where people are in the directory. Qeet ID searches under it.
drawer.filterHint: What they type replaces %s. Active Directory often uses (sAMAccountName=%s).
drawer.statusDraftHint: Nobody signs in with it until you've tested it and turned it on.
drawer.statusOnHint: People can sign in with it straight away.

required.name: Enter a name.
required.serverUrl: Enter an address that starts with ldap:// or ldaps://.
required.filter: Put %s where the name they type goes.

on.done: {{name}} is on: people can sign in with it

off.title: Turn off {{name}}?
off.description: People can't sign in with their password from {{host}} until you turn it back on. Their accounts stay as they are.

delete.zoneOn: People who sign in with it will need another way in.
delete.zoneOff: It isn't on, so nobody signs in with it now.
delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.description: People can no longer sign in with their password from {{host}}. Their accounts, groups and roles stay; anyone who signs in only this way needs another way in. Its sync history stays in Activity.
